title: DeviceDescription
description:
A device as a protocol describes it. The core adds it to the registry, or updates the
entry with the same `unique_id`.

connections.description:
Hardware addresses and serial numbers the device is known by, for an extension that
reaches devices another extension may reach too, such as a bridge to another hub. The
core uses them only to recognise the same device found twice (`docs/specs/protocols.md`
§6.1); an extension that talks to its devices directly leaves this empty.

serial_number.description: The serial number the device reports for itself.

suggested_area.description:
An area name the device reports for itself, e.g. ESPHome's `area`. The core uses it only
when the device is new and the user hasn't assigned an area.

unique_id.description: The protocol's permanent handle for the device, e.g. its MAC address.

via_device_unique_id.description: The `unique_id` of the bridge or hub this device is reached through.

Connection.description:
One identifier a device is known by beyond its protocol's `unique_id`. Its value is kept
normalized, so two spellings of one address are equal: a MAC or IEEE address in lowercase
with no separators or `0x` (`AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF` is `aabbccddeeff`), a serial number trimmed.

ConnectionKind.description: What kind of identifier a [`Connection`] is.

oneOf.description: A MAC address (EUI-48), e.g. a Wi-Fi, Ethernet or Bluetooth address.
An IEEE address (EUI-64), e.g. a Zigbee or Thread device's.
The serial number the maker gave it.

Name.description: A human-readable name. 1-100 characters, no leading or trailing whitespace.

UniqueId.description: Stable id assigned by the protocol (e.g. a Zigbee IEEE address). Unique within the protocol.
